fieldNotes.siteResolution: Supplied coords (43.5803,-85.2097) had a wrong longitude and landed in farmland ~21 km east of the plant. Google geocode of the street address (19275 8 Mile Rd, Stanwood MI 49346) returned 43.58243,-85.46877; satellite there shows the large (~411k sq ft) Ice Mountain / Nestle Waters / BlueTriton-Primo bottling plant. Locked building-area center 43.58110,-85.46640. The 8 Mile Rd / diagonal county road forms the north property frontage; the private truck drive runs south off it into the yard.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed from Street View (pano dM-z9Dmn3ZPJxyeq-N9leg, captured 2025-07, at the drive mouth 43.58389,-85.46680 looking S): a chain-link slide/swing gate spans the private truck drive ~80 m in from the public road, with a perimeter fence line, a stop sign on a post mid-drive, a tall light pole, and a card-reader/call-box pole at the gate. Clear controlled checkpoint. True.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No large multi-window staffed booth visible. There is a small (~1-vehicle-footprint) white-roofed structure beside the drive at the gate (z21 43.5832,-85.4670), but it reads as a check-in kiosk / call-box shelter rather than a manned guard booth; SV shows signage and a card-reader pole, not a window-walled booth. Marked false (low confidence).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: True: there IS a controlled truck gate but no confirmed staffed guard shack, implying kiosk / call-box / card-reader check-in (the pole + stop sign seen in SV at the gate). Low confidence, paired with the guardShack call.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide internal paved apron between the gate and the dock faces plus the large internal yard easily holds queued trucks inside the fence before the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long private approach (~80-120 m gate-to-dock) plus a deep internal yard -> holds well over 3 trucks queued.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: South wall of the main building is a continuous long dock bank with many doors and trailers backed in across the full length (south-dock z19, z18); the building's east/NE face carries a second dock bank with trailers backed in (east z17). Honest overhead estimate ~58 total -> 50+ band. Exact count uncertain due to building length and apron trailers obscuring some bays.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Dedicated drop yard east of the building (dropyard2 z18, eastend z18): multiple long rows of parked trailers without tractors, ~60-80 in marked rows -> 50+ band.
fieldNotes.dropYard: True - a distinct, dedicated trailer-storage lot east of the plant, separate from the active dock-apron staging.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Two physically distinct dock clusters on different building faces (long south-face bank + east/NE-face bank) suggest separate shipping/receiving operations, but function cannot be confirmed from imagery -> medium confidence.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single truck drive off the public road serving both in and out at one point on the north property line.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single inbound lane at the gate from imagery; exit shares the same drive. Banded entry=exit=1.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Single-lane gate with no obvious spare paved width for a bypass; the approach is rural with low backup risk, so no fast-lane need flagged. False.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Gate sits ~80 m back from a low-traffic rural county road behind a deep approach -> a truck queue would stack on the private drive, not the public road. False.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural - open farmland and woods surround the plant near the small village of Stanwood, Mecosta County; only the plant and a small adjacent industrial cluster are developed.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Although rural, the site is an active large-scale industrial plant on a county road with a neighboring industrial cluster and on-prem infrastructure; cellular coverage is reasonable. False (would be borderline; flagged-adjacent).
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: A separate small building cluster (white pole-barn warehouses with their own trailers) sits immediately NE across the yard (dropyard z18, dropyard2 z18). It looks like an adjacent/secondary operation rather than a second large building of the same plant, so multipleFacilities=false for the Ice Mountain plant itself, but it is a campus-adjacent cluster - flagged uncertain. buildingCount=2 counts the main plant plus this attached NE warehouse mass.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh pad with scale house identified in the truck path. False.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property; access is road-only. False.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~60-80 in the east drop yard rows + ~20 in the south apron + ~25-30 backed into docks = ~105. Approximate; dense rows and mixed imagery vintages make this a high-confidence-band, low-confidence-exact count.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Drop-yard rows hold ~80-100; apron and internal yard push practical capacity to ~120.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: ~32 acres of fenced active yard + building footprint derived from the perimeter polygon (front pond/grass buffer to the public road excluded); ~484 m E-W x ~312 m N-S bounding extent.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main plant is one very large connected structure; counted 2 to include the distinct attached NE warehouse mass / adjacent cluster.
fieldNotes.imageryQuality: Maxar/Airbus tiles are sharp at z17-z19; Street View (2025-07) covers the public road and the drive mouth and clearly shows the gate, but Google did not drive past the gate, so the booth-vs-kiosk distinction and exact dock count are the main residual uncertainties.
